extracted.intended_audience: appellants, respondents, lawyers, registrars and administrators involved in appeals to the PAB (CPP/QPP/Unemployment Insurance)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and practical guidance for instituting, preparing, hearing, and deciding appeals before the PAB under the CPP, QPP and Unemployment Insurance Acts, including filing, interventions, evidence, hearings, and decision requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum and authorization for appeals from the Umpire
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAB must authorize any appeal against a decision rendered by the Umpire; like any other decision of the PAB, the decision must be handed down by a quorum of three members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although statutory provisions may be imprecise, practice follows the same PAB rules of procedure; in practice the PAB has never refused leave to appeal claimants in unemployment insurance contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for appealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Most provisions creating a right of appeal to the PAB fix the time limit for appealing at 90 days; no time limit is specified for appeals in the sphere of unemployment insurance contributions, and section 86 of the Unemployment Insurance Act is exceptional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 90-day limit runs from notification of the contested decision; in areas where leave to appeal is not required, the notice must be filed within 90 days following the challenged decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of the time limit for appealing
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAB or one of its members may grant an extension of the time limit for appealing; rules differ as to when an application for extension must be presented (e.g., CPP/QPP distinctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAB insists on valid and serious reasons for failure to comply with statutory time limits (not mere neglect); the application for extension must set out reasons and specify additional time requested; the Chairman rules on extensions on their merits and, for CPP benefits, upon review of the case file transmitted by the Review Committee. Refusals are accompanied by reasons in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and filing of the notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must identify the date, nature and subject of the challenged decision, as well as the arguments of fact and law invoked by the appellant in support of his contention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the PAB practices considerable flexibility and will accept notices that do not fully meet these requirements, the formal requirements remain. Upon receipt the Registrar notifies the other party; when the Minister is the other party he must transmit initiating documents and a list of parties who were notified so the Registrar can advise them of intervention rights. The Registrar also transmits a copy of the rules of procedure to the public party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar's duty on receipt of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the notice of appeal the Registrar notifies the other party and transmits applicable rules of procedure to parties, and if the Minister is involved, the Registrar receives initiating documents and lists of parties from the Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables the Registrar to advise notified parties of their right to intervene and to ensure the file contains the initiating documents required for the PAB's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of the appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for withdrawal differ by area; no provision is made for withdrawal in contributions, while benefits rules specify how to express intention but are silent on legal effects; PAB practice authorizes the Registrar to issue an order declaring the appellant has manifested intention to withdraw, ending the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial numbers of appeals are withdrawn before hearing; parties often lodge appeals hastily and later lose interest, are intimidated, or recognize weak arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Registrar in preparations
rubrics_metrics.description: During the preparation phase the Registrar ensures written submissions conform to rules, provides guidance through administrative procedure, and encourages active participation by parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registrar also determines the time and place of hearings (in consultation) and is responsible for organizing sittings across regions, notifying parties, and entering the case on the PAB rolls when ready for adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — who may intervene and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person having an interest in the case whom the Registrar has informed of the receipt of a notice of appeal has the right to intervene or to file a cross-appeal; in contributions cases intervenors are limited to those notified by the Registrar (i.e., those invited by the Minister).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervenors may appropriate other parties' arguments or present their own; PAB may require duplicated intervenors to consolidate into a single intervention to abbreviate proceedings; third-party interventions are possible if authorized by the Chairman. The Registrar transmits rules of procedure to potential intervenors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules of Procedure prescribe time limits for filing interventions: 30 days for appeals concerning contributions and 20 days for appeals concerning benefits, running from Registrar notification of the receipt of a notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are treated with some practical elasticity due to administrative delays and the informal spirit of the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to the notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent declares his position regarding facts alleged and indicates the arguments he intends to rely on at hearing; filing a reply marks termination of written exchanges and readiness for adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits: in contributions cases the Minister must file his reply within 30 days after the interventions period; in benefits cases the time limit is 20 days from the Registrar's notification. If no reply is filed, the appellant may request an ex parte hearing, though defendant may still file a late reply and PAB may authorize belated filing in certain benefits cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement before the hearing and ratification
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to settle issues before the hearing; even when settled, a PAB judgment is necessary to reverse the Review Committee's decision and the matter is entered on the rolls for ratification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Minister's legal representative submits settlement terms to the PAB for ratification by summary decision; such summary decisions are not published, making exact proportions of out-of-court settlements difficult to determine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other pre-hearing incidents (discovery and consolidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAB may authorize examination for discovery of any party by another with authorization; consolidation of appeals is a more frequent device used to hear appeals together for convenience and expeditiousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is seldom used; consolidation may be justified by common questions of law or fact or generally in 'the interests of justice' and can involve appeals under the same Act or across Acts (e.g., CPP & QPP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for determining time and place of hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectively the PAB (with leadership by the Chairman) determines the time and place of hearings; in practice the Registrar consults members and parties and accommodates schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearings are typically arranged in large urban centres for access and premises; logistical difficulties due to member dispersion make scheduling burdensome. The Registrar must give parties at least 20 days' notice of time and place by letter and telephone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that appeals (contributions) be ruled on after a hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: For contribution matters the Rules of Procedure prescribe that appeals will be ruled on following a hearing; although some Acts permit decisions based on the file alone, PAB practice has been to give an actual hearing where parties act with due diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CPP expressly alludes to presence of PAB members at the hearing; QPP and UI Acts allow possible decision on the file, but PAB historically gives hearings in contribution cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity of hearings and in-camera requests
rubrics_metrics.description: PAB hearings are public, at least in benefits cases; a party may request the case be heard in camera for special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicity for contribution hearings is not explicitly laid down, but PAB generally follows the same rule while protecting privacy of business transactions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation, representation and restrictions on representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries commonly attend or are represented (often by lawyers); parties may ask for adjournments but should not do so lightly; the PAB will not permit a person who previously acted on the Review Committee whose decision is challenged to plead the beneficiary's case before the PAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High rates of lawyer representation in contributions cases; absences without excuse may lead to ex parte proceedings. Requests for adjournment are problematic because reassembling the same PAB members is often difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standards at hearing (oral primacy, witnesses, disqualifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAB maintains flexibility but in principle the proof offered must be oral evidence though other proof types may be authorized; PAB can summon witnesses who testify under oath; a member of the Review Committee whose decision is challenged is ineligible to testify, though the Committee's secretary may testify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral testimony often has greater weight than written certificates (notably physician testimony vs signed certificates). The Minister routinely provides medical experts, sometimes producing physicians who examined the claimant; this can disadvantage claimants who seldom produce attending physicians as witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter and language accommodations and cost allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a defendant or third party is obviously incapable of testifying in English or French in appeals lodged by the Minister, the Minister must provide an interpreter at his own expense; where the appeal is initiated by the beneficiary, interpretation costs are charged to the beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one aspect of the broader issue of reimbursing parties for hearing-related expenses; language issues particularly affect recent immigrants with limited expression in official languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement of travel and legal expenses (CPP section 88)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 88 entitles parties requested by the PAB to participate to be paid travelling and other allowances, including compensation for loss of remuneration; section 88(2) provides for repayment of legal expenses to a respondent beneficiary or the second claimant for a surviving spouse if represented by a lawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reimbursement is available only where statutory conditions are met (e.g., representation by a lawyer for legal fees); the Registrar notifies parties likely to benefit of these provisions when hearing dates are set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and completeness of the case file
rubrics_metrics.description: The case file prepared for the hearing should contain: the original application (for benefits, determination or decision), the initial administrative decision with reasons, communications initiating internal review, decisions following internal review with reasons, communications initiating contentious review (notices to Review Committee or Umpire), replies and interventions, documents produced before the lower appeal authority, minutes (where applicable), decision of the lower appeal authority with reasons, communications initiating the appeal to the PAB and documents placed on file by the parties before the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case files are often supplemented during the hearing (e.g., recent medical exam reports) and completeness is essential for proper adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing between roll entry and hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing generally takes place approximately one month after the case is entered on the rolls of the PAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interval from notice of appeal to entry on the rolls (preparation phase) often averages many months (e.g., ~312–342 days in CPP cases) reflecting practical delays; once on the rolls, hearings are scheduled relatively promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and communication of the PAB decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Except under the Unemployment Insurance Act, the Acts conferring jurisdiction on the PAB require that decisions be in writing, have reasons assigned to them, and be communicated to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formal requirement ensures reasons are provided; summary decisions ratifying settlements are not published, however.
